'''Mullan''' was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|world]]<ref name="Xim" /> located in the [[Mullan system/Legends|Mullan system]].<ref name="TEA" /> It was a part of the [[Keldrath sector/Legends|Keldrath sector]] in the [[Greater Tion]] historical region,<ref name="Xim" /> which in turn was situated within [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TEA" /> The [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] known as the [[Pakuuni Drift]] connected Mullan to the [[Gbu system/Legends|Gbu system]] as well as the [[Brigia system/Legends|Brigia system]] in the neighboring [[Tion Hegemony/Legends|Tion Hegemony]] [[Sector/Legends|sector]].<ref name="Xim" />

[[Homeworld/Legends|Home]] to the [[mullanite]] [[Plant/Legends|plant]],<ref name="Guide" /><ref name="Planetnamia" /> Mullan had been well-known for a long [[Time/Legends|time]] for its placid population as well as for the hearty [[Foodstuff/Legends|foodstuffs]] and simple [[Wine/Legends|wines]] the natives were exporting. Mullan managed to escape the long and turbulent history of the Greater Tion, and served as the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of the Keldrath sector, which was established by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="Xim" />

==Behind the scenes==
Mullan was introduced as a map label in the<ref name="TEA" /> [[August 18]], [[2009]]<ref name="Penguin">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/185066/the-essential-atlas-star-wars-by-daniel-wallace-and-jason-fry|text=The Essential Atlas: Star Wars}}</ref> reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', authored by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]]. The book placed the Mullan [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore Mullan itself, in grid square T-6.<ref name="TEA" /> The [[December 7]], 2009 [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]]<ref name="XimOriginal">{{SWArchive|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek01/index.html|text=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster|int=Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster}}</ref> article "[[Xim Week: The History of Xim and the Tion Cluster]]" by Fry first identified Mullan as a distinct world.<ref name="Xim" />
